items.evidence: The walk passes in both browsers. Mutation proof in a scratch worktree (removed afterwards): an offer was injected into each listed screen/dialog in turn, and each walk failed naming it. Home text 'Deposit' -> home; Game Config title attr 'Buy chips' -> game-config; Game Config hidden <option>Purchase -> game-config; End-session dialog text 'Cash out' -> end-session-dialog; Table aria-label 'Top up' -> table; hint card 'Pay now' -> table; review panel 'Play for real money' -> table ("real money"); Bust dialog 'Withdraw' -> bust-dialog; ending main text 'Deposit' and an aria-label 'Credit card' -> ending; Report hidden input value 'Redeem chips' -> session-report ("Redeem"). WebKit re-run of the end-session, review, bust and ending injections was also caught. Registering an extra entry without walking it failed with 'screen list entries not visited: stats'. The same-origin request assertion is present (requests > 0 and every origin is http://localhost:4173). Recorded deviation: hand 14 is played with call so the review opens (qa.md), which is consistent with REQ-043.12.

tests/ui/screen-list.acceptance.test.ts passes on the real repo and also asserts the found routes and dialogs exactly. Mutation: adding a 'stats' Screen member plus a new src/ui/settings/SettingsDialog.tsx with role="dialog" failed with both 'dialog SettingsDialog is not in the screen list' and 'screen stats is not in the screen list'. A native <dialog> file alone failed naming the dialog. Removing <dialog> from BustDialog failed with 'screen list entry bust-dialog matches no screen or dialog in the app'. The holdout real-source comparison returned [] and named new entries.

The unit test asserts the exact 3 sorted messages and the ConfirmBox alertdialog detection. Holdout checks: only the Screen union is read (nested braces, double quotes and duplicates handled, sorted), and role='dialog', role=dialog, Windows paths and duplicate <dialog> tags are detected. role="dialogue", <dialogs> and aria-label="dialog" are not detected. A missing Screen type makes every screen entry stale. A dialog mis-registered as a screen is reported as both unlisted and stale. All pass.

The bundle test passes on the real dist/ and asserts at least one .js file. Mutations caught: adding new PaymentRequest plus a fetch of https://js.stripe.com/v3 to src/main.tsx gave ['assets/index-*.js: Payment Request API (PaymentRequest)', 'assets/index-*.js: payment-provider URL (js.stripe.com)']. A paypal preconnect in index.html gave 'index.html: payment-provider URL (www.paypal.com)'. Adding @stripe/stripe-js to package.json dependencies gave 'package.json: payment library @stripe/stripe-js'.

The unit test asserts the exact spec output and the clean case. Holdout checks: API findings across files come first, then URLs, then libraries. .html and .css files are scanned, and PaymentResponse is found. Scoped and dev/peer packages are found; squared and a non-object dependencies field are ignored. pay.google.com and apple-pay-gateway.apple.com are found. Look-alikes (mystripe.com, stripe.company, paypal.comx, MyPaymentRequestX, pay.google.co) are not flagged. All pass.

The fixture test passes in both browsers and asserts the exact message 'Play-money check failed on fixture-deposit: "Deposit"' for both the text button and the aria-label-only icon button. It maps resolve to 'passed', so it cannot pass vacuously. The real collector's attribute, option and input coverage was confirmed by the SPEC-01 injections.

The unit test checks every row of the worked-example table with toEqual. Holdout positives were all matched as written: withdrawal, PURCHASE, Checkout, Payment, Pay with, Pay online, Buy now, buy more chips, Buy coins/credits/tokens, Real-cash, realmoney, Cash-outs, Topup, Convert winnings, converting to money, Exchange chips/winnings, Debit card, Card number, and the brand names. Holdout negatives were all clean: pay, cash, wager, Bet, Raise, All-in, Buy-in, payday, prepaid, payout ratio, cashier, topped, striped, Rebuy for $160, and others. Repeated calls give the same result (no global-regex lastIndex leakage). False-positive sweep: every string in src/**/*.json (strategy and bot content) and every literal or JSX text in src .ts/.tsx (more than 200 strings) gave zero matches.

lint, typecheck and npm test pass (boundary and golden suites included). The playtest of 10000 hands with seed 42 reports 'Invariant violations: 0'. The play-money e2e spec passes. CI on the branch is green: runs 45467875600 (de21cec) and 45468942933 (d7ad897, HEAD), plus Visual. docs/ui/play-money.md documents the phrase list, the screen list table, the registration steps and the commands. It is not yet in `backlog doc list`; in this workflow publishing happens in the post-judge docs step (as for TASK-2.7), so this is not counted as a failure.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: a future dialog component is found however its role is written. Actual: a role given as a JSX expression (role={'dialog'}) is not detected. This matches the spec's A-3 regex exactly, so it is not a spec violation (the code reviewer raised the same MINOR point).
findings.fix: Optional follow-up: also accept role={'dialog'} / role={"alertdialog"} in the dialog detector.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: docs/ui/play-money.md published to Backlog.md. Actual: not yet published at judge time (normally done in the docs + done step).

summary: All 8 SPEC items PASS. The suite is green (1259 passed), and the e2e spec passes 6/6 in Chromium and WebKit in 2.7 s. Mutation testing in a removed scratch worktree showed the walk catches an injected offer on every listed screen and dialog (including the hint card, the review panel, the transient ending screen, and attribute-, option- and input-only text) and names the screen. The source-vs-list check names a new route, a new dialog and a stale entry. The bundle scan catches Payment Request API use and a provider URL in JS and HTML, and a payment package in package.json. There are no false positives on the real app's poker text, integrity is clean, and CI is green on HEAD. Only LOW findings.
